increaseLifespan.comment: mTOR overactivation contributes to impaired autophagy, and that inhibition of mTOR partially recovers autophagy and S6K1 activity in Zmpste24−/− mice. Zmpste24−/−mTOR△/+ mice with genetic reduction of mTOR grow to a larger size than their Zmpste24−/− littermates. The median onset of abnormal grip strength of Zmpste24−/− mTOR△/+ mice was delayed to 95 days, compared to 59 days for Zmpste24−/− mTOR+/+ mice, an extension of 61%. mTOR△/+ mice are born at normal Mendelian’ ratio. In the Zmpste24−/− background, 79.5% of mTOR△/+ mice fail to develop normally in utero.

increaseLifespan.comment:
dTORFRB is a dominant negative form of TOR. It carries TED (toxic effector domain), containing the 754 amino acid central region, which inhibits cell growth and arrests cells in G1 when overexpressed in yeast. Ubiquitous overexpression with the da-GAL4 driver of UAS-dTORFRB led to a mean life-span increase at 29°C of 24%.
Overexpression of UAS-dTORWT (full-length wild-type TOR gene) or UAS-dTORTED (another dominant-negative form) prevented eclosion to adulthood (data not shown).

experiment.interventionMethod: addition to the genome of a dominant-negative gene variant that reduces the activity of an endogenous protein

ageRelatedChangesOfGene.comment:
Without modification no significant differences were identified in the levels of mTOR among the experimental groups.
The expression level of phosphorylated mTOR decreases with age: compared to 3 months in the adult 1 group (6 months) a decrease of 32% was revealed.
Compared to 3 months in the adult group 2 (12 months) a 41% decrease in phosphorylated mTOR was revealed.
Compared with 3 months, a 56% decrease in phosphorylated mTOR was detected in the group of old animals (24 months).

interventionToGeneImprovesVitalProcesses.comment:
The effect of mTOR inhibition by RAD001 on immunosenescence (the decline in immune function during aging) was studied.
The investigation included 218 elderly volunteers (≥65 years old, without unstable medical conditions) who took placebo or RAD001 orally for 6 weeks according to one of three protocols: 0.5 mg per day, 5 mg per week or 20 mg per week. After a 2-week interval without medication, the patients received a vaccine against the 2012 seasonal flu.
RAD001 increased the response to the flu vaccine by about 20%, and also reduced the percentage of CD4 and CD8 T-lymphocytes expressing the PD-1 receptor.

commentEvolution: mTOR is a gene encoding a serine-threonine specificity protein kinase (also called the "mammalian target of rapamycin"). The gene, as well as the entire TOR signaling pathway, is highly conserved. Targets of rapamycin (mTOR orthologs) and the TOR signaling pathway are present in all animals, as well as in yeast (in yeast, 2 genes encode the TOR signaling pathway) [10.1038/onc.2012.567]. Presumably, the gene originated during the early evolution of eukaryotes [10.1126/scisignal. 2000803].
